summary: Gone 12x12 frame cabin near Sawyer Ridge, Idaho County: built about 1924, destroyed 1950; no staffing or site description found; Sawyer Ridge may have replaced it.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1950 according to all three sources; no source describes what remains at the site.
facts.agency: Nez Perce National Forest (Idaho Fire Lookouts adds Clearwater)

events.note: 12-by-12-foot frame cabin with roof platform; dated about 1924 (c.1924 on Forest Lookouts)

evidence.supports: two miles north of Sawyer Ridge Lookout, not on a prominent point
evidence.quote: Two miles north of Sawyer Ridge Lookout, and not on a prominent point

evidence.supports: does not yet have a documented staffing history
evidence.quote: We don't yet have a documented staffing history for this lookout.

evidence.supports: may have been replaced by Sawyer Ridge Lookout to the south
evidence.quote: It may have been replaced by Sawyer Ridge Lookout 2 miles to the south.

evidence.supports: c.1924 12x12 frame cabin with roof platform
evidence.quote: c.1924: 12x12 frame cabin with roof platform.

evidence.supports: Sawyer Ridge may have been a replacement site for Marble Point
evidence.quote: may have been a replacement site for Marble Point Lookout 2 miles to the north

evidence.supports: built 1949 as a 41-foot treated timber tower with L-4 cab
evidence.quote: Originally constructed in 1949, the 41' treated timber tower with L-4 cab

corrections.why: Idaho is the state; firelookout.com gives Idaho County, Idaho and the Forest Lookouts page lists IDAHO COUNTY

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com names the Nez Perce National Forest; Idaho Fire Lookouts names the Clearwater/Nez Perce National Forest. The record keeps Nez Perce.

notes_for_editor: Sources agree on the about-1924 cabin and the 1950 destruction. The Sawyer Ridge replacement link is only a 'may have' in two sources, and Sawyer's 1949 date falls before 1950; do not treat it as established, and check it against any Sawyer Ridge record. Elevation 5,983 ft appears in two sources; the record's elevation_m is empty. The drive-up label describes the cabin as it stood, not a visit fact.
